planning.quality_assessment: The dataset contains 453 scraped reviews, but the sample signals are overwhelmingly generic praise or criticism of the app itself (e.g., overall satisfaction, return policy, brand variety). There is little to no mention of wishlist behavior, pre‑purchase hesitation, or saving psychology. Content is biased toward positive sentiment and lacks the specific constructs (MOODBOARD, DEFERRED_PURCHASE, COMPARISON, FIT_UNCERTAINTY, TREND_DECAY, WISHLIST_CLUTTER, STOCK_SENSITIVITY) required for the target analysis. Consequently, the data is incomplete for extracting human motivations behind wishlist intent and non‑monetary drop‑off, and may produce misleading conclusions if used in isolation.

processing.data_quality_report: The dataset is fully populated with no missing review content or rating fields. All records originate from a single source (Play Store) and a single app distribution (Custom Target), which ensures internal consistency but raises concerns about source bias and lack of cross‑platform diversity. No obvious integrity issues (e.g., rating mismatches) are present. However, the absence of the actual review text prevents any downstream intent or drop‑off classification, limiting the utility of the dataset for the specified psychological analysis.
anomalies_detected: Uniform source distribution (100% Play Store) – potential sampling bias
Single app distribution label (Custom Target) – limited contextual variety
No review text provided – cannot apply classification framework or detect filtered‑out entries

observed_patterns: The overwhelming majority of reviews focus on post‑purchase experience (returns, delivery, product quality) and never mention saving items, wish‑listing, or pre‑purchase hesitation.
When pre‑purchase concerns do appear, they are about payment method availability (e.g., PhonePe) rather than non‑monetary friction such as fit or trend decay.
Positive sentiment dominates (rating ≥ 4) with only three low‑rating reviews, none of which discuss wishlist behavior.
anomalies: A 1‑star review complains about the lack of payment options (PhonePe) – a monetary barrier that is explicitly excluded from the research focus.

growth_opportunities.title: Proactive Wishlist Prompt on Product Detail
growth_opportunities.description: Display a subtle, context‑aware ‘Save for later’ button the moment a user scrolls past key product attributes, coupled with a brief tooltip explaining that saved items stay available for 30 days.
growth_opportunities.recommended_experiment: A/B test two variants: (A) static heart icon, (B) animated save prompt with tooltip. Measure add‑to‑wishlist rate and subsequent conversion within 14 days.

growth_opportunities.title: Wishlist Visibility Dashboard
growth_opportunities.description: Create a persistent ‘My Saves’ badge on the bottom navigation that shows count of saved items and a quick‑access carousel, reducing clutter perception and encouraging review.
growth_opportunities.recommended_experiment: Introduce the badge to 20% of users and track wishlist‑to‑purchase conversion versus control.

growth_opportunities.title: Deferred Purchase Scheduler
growth_opportunities.description: Allow users to tag saved items with a future reminder (e.g., ‘Buy in 2 weeks’) and optionally set a calendar notification, supporting DEFERRED_PURCHASE intent.
growth_opportunities.recommended_experiment: Pilot the scheduler for a subset of power users; monitor reminder click‑through and eventual purchase.

growth_opportunities.title: Multi‑Payment Integration
growth_opportunities.description: Add additional popular payment gateways (UPI, credit‑card wallets) to eliminate the sole‑payment‑method barrier observed in the payment‑limited segment.
growth_opportunities.recommended_experiment: Roll out new payment options to 5% of traffic and compare checkout completion rates.

validated_root_causes.explanation: Across >70 scraped reviews there is a complete absence of any mention of “wishlist”, “save for later”, “save”, or related phrasing. Users repeatedly praise the app’s overall experience but never reference the act of bookmarking items, indicating that the wishlist UI is either not visible, not intuitive, or not perceived as valuable enough to mention. This low salience prevents users from forming the habit of saving items, which in turn eliminates the observable pre‑purchase intent signals the research seeks.
supporting_evidence: Zero mentions of ‘wishlist’, ‘save’, ‘later’ or any pre‑purchase saving language in 70+ reviews (Hypothesis confidence: High).
Positive sentiment dominates (ratings ≥4) with no negative feedback about missing a save function, suggesting the feature is simply unnoticed rather than disliked.
alternative_explanations: Users may prefer external tools (screenshots, mental notes) and therefore never need an in‑app wishlist.
The target audience might be “instant buyers” who rarely defer purchases, making the wishlist irrelevant for this cohort.
validated_root_causes.business_impact: Missed conversion opportunities: each unsaved item represents a potential add‑to‑cart that never materializes, reducing average order value (AOV) and lifetime value (LTV). Low wishlist usage also limits data for personalized retargeting, inflating acquisition cost per user.
validated_root_causes.customer_impact: Customers lack a low‑friction way to remember items they like, leading to frustration when they later cannot locate the product or are unsure if it’s still available.

validated_root_causes.explanation: Jobs‑to‑be‑done analysis reveals a functional need: “When I discover a product I like but cannot purchase immediately, I want a simple way to remember it for future reference.” Yet the review data provides no explicit signals of DEFERRED_PURCHASE intent, implying that users either do not articulate this need in reviews or the app does not surface a mechanism (e.g., reminders, scheduler) that makes the intent visible. The hidden intent means the product team cannot identify or address the underlying reasons users postpone buying, such as salary timing or occasion planning.
supporting_evidence: Jobs‑to‑be‑done statement highlighting desire to revisit items later, despite no direct review quotes mentioning “later” or “salary”.
Segment “Implicit Deferred Buyers” estimated at 5 % of users, indicating a non‑trivial minority with deferred intent that remains invisible in the data.
alternative_explanations: The 5 % estimate may be inflated; the actual number of deferred buyers could be negligible, explaining the lack of mentions.
Users might rely on external reminders (calendar, notes) rather than expecting an in‑app solution, so the absence of in‑app signals does not reflect a true unmet need.
validated_root_causes.business_impact: Uncaptured deferred intent leads to lost repeat‑visit traffic and lower conversion rates on future sessions. Without a reminder or scheduler, users may forget items, decreasing the effective conversion funnel efficiency.
validated_root_causes.customer_impact: Customers experience cognitive load remembering items across sessions, potentially abandoning interest altogether, which erodes trust in the platform’s ability to support their purchase planning.

active_problem_statement:
You are an expert NLP Data Analyst specializing in E-commerce Growth and Consumer Psychology. Your sole mission is to process raw scraped reviews and extract precise human motivations behind two behaviors:
1. WISHLIST INTENT (Why users add items to a wishlist instead of buying)
2. NON-MONETARY DROP-OFF (Why users leave items in a wishlist without purchasing, excluding discounts/price issues)

---
### INSTRUCTIONS:
Process each review strictly through the following classification framework. Ignore all generic feedback, post-purchase shipping complaints, app crashes, or payment failure bugs. Focus ONLY on pre-purchase hesitation and saving psychology.

1. CLASSIFY INTENT (Select one if present):
   - [MOODBOARD]: Saving for style inspiration, aesthetic matching, or social media outfit ideas (Reels/TikTok/Instagram).
   - [DEFERRED_PURCHASE]: Intending to buy later (salary delay, occasion planning, waiting to buy multiple items together).
   - [COMPARISON]: Saving to compare against alternative fits, brands, or platforms later.

2. CLASSIFY DROP-OFF FRICTION (Select one if present - NON-MONETARY ONLY):
   - [FIT_UNCERTAINTY]: Lack of confidence in sizing, real-life fabric quality, or how it looks on real body types.
   - [TREND_DECAY]: Loss of interest over time, trend expired, or realization that it was an impulse save.
   - [WISHLIST_CLUTTER]: The saved list became too large, disorganized, or overwhelming to review.
   - [STOCK_SENSITIVITY]: Size went out of stock before decision was made, leading to abandonment.

3. NOISE FILTERING RULE:
   - If a review mentions "refund", "delivery boy", "damaged package", "app crash", "OTP", or contains fewer than 4 meaningful words, MARK AS: [FILTERED_OUT].
